title: Kartini's birth chart
metaDescription: Kartini's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 0.7° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mercury holds a sextile to Mars at 0.1° — close enough to weld thinking to drive. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 0.7° into Taurus — the first decan, which the old scheme hands to Venus. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 24.4° Aries, Venus holds 2.9° Gemini, Mars holds 24.6° Aquarius — in the old shorthand, thought that arrives already in motion; attraction that begins as conversation; effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mercury to Mars, a sextile with 0.1° of slack. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, the Sun trine Uranus at 0.5°, and Mars square Pluto at 0.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Uranus while both square Venus. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. Saturn makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Jupiter in Pisces at 5.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Aries at 8.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in earth, 2 in fire, 2 in air, 1 in water by element, 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal by modality. Mercury and Uranus were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.9° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
